questions.q: What does the European Superintendent at Ezenzeleni do that is 'not the custom'?
questions.explain: Msimangu has evidently spoken to him privately, and Kumalo is left in peace to rest.

questions.q: What happens to Kumalo as he sits for hours in the sun above the wide plain?
choices: He falls asleep and misses the service
There is 'some rising of the spirit, some lifting of the fear'
He decides to give up the search
questions.explain: He begins to accept Msimangu's point: why fear this one thing in a city of thousands upon thousands?

questions.q: As he sits, what does Kumalo finally admit to himself about the tribe?
choices: That it can be fully restored
That 'the tribe was broken, and would be mended no more'
That the chief will save it
That the mines will save it
questions.explain: It feels 'as though a man borne upward into the air felt suddenly that the wings of miracle dropped away from him.'

questions.q: What thoughts of rebuilding comfort Kumalo?
choices: Buying a farm on the tops
That if Absalom and the girl marry, they might come back to Ndotsheni and he could give the child what he failed to give his own son
questions.explain: He also resolves to return with 'a new and quickened interest in the school.'

questions.q: What does Msimangu say to Kumalo when he comes to fetch him for food?
choices: 'It is time to turn. This is madness... But it is also sin. I speak to you as a priest.'
'We must leave at once for the prison.'
questions.explain: Kumalo answers, 'You are right, father. I must sit here no longer.'

questions.q: What work is done at Ezenzeleni?
choices: White men, some English- and some Afrikaans-speaking, help black people who are blind — teaching them to make baskets
questions.explain: 'It was white men who did this work of mercy... came together to open the eyes of black men that were blind.'

questions.q: What is remarkable about Msimangu's voice as he reads and preaches in the chapel?
choices: It is 'of gold' — Kumalo had not known his friend had such a voice
questions.explain: 'It was not only a voice of gold, but it was the voice of a man whose heart was golden.'

questions.q: From which book of the Bible does Msimangu read to the blind?
choices: Isaiah — 'To open the blind eyes, to bring out the prisoners from the prison'
questions.explain: Kumalo hears it as spoken to him: 'we are not forsaken.'

questions.q: Which promise from the reading especially lifts Kumalo?
choices: 'They that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles'
'I am the way, the truth and the life'
questions.explain: 'The people sigh, and Kumalo sighs, as though this is a great word that has been spoken.'

questions.q: How does Kumalo greet Msimangu after the service?
choices: 'You should not have brought me here.'
questions.explain: Msimangu answers humbly that he had tried every way to touch Kumalo but could not come near — 'So give thanks and be satisfied.'
